newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaeval wall collapses in Italian city.
newsitem.headline: Mediaeval wall collapses in Italian city.

text.p: A large section of the 11th century wall which encircles the Italian city of Viterbo collapsed on Monday night, officials said on Tuesday.
"A wall about 10 metres (33 feet) high and 15 metres (50 feet) long collapsed just before midnight," a spokesman for the city council said.
No injuries were reported. Another big section of the wall, which was erected in 1095, collapsed on Sunday morning.
The small mediaeval city of Viterbo lies 100 km (60 miles) north of Rome.
Much of central and southern Italy has had several months of heavy rain but city officials said it was not clear why the walls collapsed.
